Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 8:61: And further, concerning the virtue of one who guards his eyes, the verse in Parashat Kedoshim explains, in saying (Leviticus 19:4), "do not turn to idols," and so on - and we have already explained, from Rashbi, that this is a warning stated so that a person not gaze at women. Now, his virtue is that the Shechinah rests with him, and this is what it says, "I am the LORD your God" - the mention of the Name Elohim indicates this, that I, your God, rest upon you if you are careful in this. And further, it is an admonition for a person to guard his sight, for in blemishing his sight he makes himself an idol, as it is said (ibid.), "and molten gods you shall not make for yourselves," as precisely derived from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, and we shall further explain below, with God's help - and it is far better that a person make himself a vessel for holiness to rest in, and not the opposite, Heaven forfend. And further, it is possible that these three words, "I am the LORD your God," correspond to the Name "Yabak" alluded to in the three colors of the eye, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Tikkunei Zohar, page 128a), whose wording we copied at the beginning of the chapter.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 8:62: And as proof of the discourse concerning the virtue of one who guards his sight, that the Shechinah is with him, a certain master of Torah testified to me that he saw, in the kingdom of Morocco, a pious and wise man who never raises his eyes from the ground, always having "humble eyes" - and from the abundance of his piety, whoever vexed him would not complete his year, and further miraculous events happened to him, and I shall not elaborate on this.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 8:63: And with this the chapter is concluded:
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:1: In this chapter shall be explained the repair of hearing and smell. Concerning the repair of hearing, the pious author of Chovot HaLevavot wrote in the Gate of Abstinence (chapter 5), in these words: and strive afterward to stop your ear from hearing what you do not need, and separate from excessive talk, falsehood, gossip, and slander, and separate from what would bring you to rebel against God and abandon His commandments, from kinds of song and music and laughter and merriment that distract you from the commandments and good deeds - but incline your ear and hear the words of the wise, and it is said (Proverbs 15:31), "an ear that hears the reproof of life" - to this point. And his words, peace be upon him, are brief and general, and need to be detailed and explained. And so one must distance himself from hearing the voice of a woman singing, for a woman's voice is nakedness (Berachot 24a).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:2: And concerning hearing idle words, our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Ketubot 5a) what is written (Deuteronomy 23:14), "and you shall have a spike [yated] with your weapons" - that if a person hears something unfitting, he should put his finger in his ears - and this is what Rabbi Elazar said: why are a person's fingers like pegs [yetedot]? Is it because they divide, each one for its own function, as the master said, this is the little finger, this the ring finger, this the middle finger, this the index finger, and this the thumb? Rather, why are their tips sloped like pegs? So that if he hears something unfitting he may put his finger in his ears. And it was taught in the school of Rabbi Yishmael: why is the outer part of the ear hard and the earlobe soft? So that if he hears something unfitting he may fold the lobe into it. Our Rabbis taught: a person should not let his ears hear unfitting things, because they are the first of the limbs to be singed - to this point, their wording.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:3: And so one must be careful not to hear slander and not to accept it, for one who accepts it [sins] more than the one who says it, as shall be explained. Further, one must be careful not to "stop his ear from the cry," and so on (Proverbs 21:13).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:4: Further, one must be careful concerning what the prophet Isaiah, peace be upon him, said (Isaiah 33:15), among the good qualities the Sages enumerated (Makkot 24a), which are the foundations of Torah and commandments - one of them being (Isaiah 33:15), "who stops his ears from hearing of bloodshed," such as Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon, and the story is told in Bava Metzia (84b) - and from there is great proof that he would not stay silent when he heard the disgrace of the Sages [being spoken].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:5: Further, one must be careful that if he has already heard a matter of halachah or midrash and hears it now a second time, he should not turn his ear from hearing it and say, I have already heard it - for concerning this it is said (Proverbs 28:9), "he who turns away his ear from hearing the Torah." And so they explained in the Midrash (Yalkut Mishlei, siman 937) on the verse (ibid. 5:19), "let her breasts satisfy you at all times" - in these words: "let her breasts satisfy you at all times" - so that you not say, we heard this last year, as it is said (ibid. 23:22), "and do not despise your mother when she is old" - and if you said so, I too can say to you, why do you recite the Shema twice a day, why do you pray three times a day - perhaps you are innovating something? If you mocked the words of Torah, I too shall not hear your prayer, as it is said, "he who turns away his ear from hearing the Torah, even his prayer is an abomination" - to this point, their wording.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:6: Further, among the things that blemish the sense of hearing is if one makes his voice heard by another while praying the Amidah silently - and besides what they said in the Talmud (Berachot 24b), that he is of little faith, they elaborated on his punishment in the Zohar (Parashat Vayakhel, page 209a), in these words: then an appointee is aroused who stands on the south side, whose name is Azriel the elder, and sometimes called Machniel, because he is appointed over six hundred thousand camps, and all of them are masters of wings, masters of camps full of eyes, and near them stand those camps of masters of ears, and they are called "ears" because they listen to all those who recite their prayers in a whisper, with the will of the heart, so that that prayer is not heard by another - that prayer ascends and is heard by all those called masters of ears; but if that prayer is heard by a person's own ears, no one above heeds it, and no others heed it except the one who first heard it - therefore one must be careful that people not [audibly] hear that prayer, and further, the matter of prayer is attached to the supernal world, and a matter of the supernal world need not be heard [by others]. And he says further there: when that prayer ascends in a whisper, all those six hundred thousand camps, and all those masters of eyes, and all those who heed, masters of ears, all go out and kiss that matter of prayer that ascends - this is what is written (Psalms 34:16), "the eyes of the LORD are toward the righteous, and His ears toward their cry" - "the eyes of the LORD are toward the righteous" - these are the masters of eyes below, for there are masters of eyes above; "and His ears toward their cry" - these are the masters of ears - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:7: Further, among the repairs of the ear is that if he has heard a secret, he should not reveal it, as explained in the Idra (Parashat Ha'azinu, page 294b), in these words: in this ear hang supernal secrets that do not go outward, and therefore it is bent inward, and the secret of secrets is hidden - woe to him who reveals secrets - and because this ear strikes the secrets and takes the depth within, it does not reveal secrets to those who are crooked in their ways, but only to those who are not crooked - this is what is written (Psalms 25:14), "the secret of the LORD is with those who fear Him, and He shall make known to them His covenant" - one who guards His ways and guards words - to this point, relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:8: Further, he explained there, right next to this teaching, that the sense of hearing is shared with the eyes, the nose, and the mouth, in these words: on this hole of the ears depend other holes - the holes of the eyes, the hole of the mouth, the hole of the nose. From that voice that enters the hole of the ear, if necessary it enters the holes of the eyes and tears well up from that voice; if necessary it enters the hole of the "pardashka," which is the nose, and smoke and fire go out from that voice - this is what is written (Numbers 11:1), "and the LORD heard, and His anger was kindled, and the fire of the LORD burned among them"; and if necessary that voice enters the hole of the mouth and speaks and decrees decrees from that voice - all from that voice enters the whole body and is stirred by it - on what does this all depend? On this ear. Happy is he who guards his words - concerning this it is written (Psalms 34:14), "guard your tongue from evil, and your lips from speaking deceit" - to this point. And his words are understood by the plain meaning, though there is certainly an inner secret within them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:9: And through this we understand what they said, of blessed memory (Bava Kamma 85b), "one who deafens him pays the full value of him [as a slave]," because all his limbs are found nullified [by deafness]. And according to his words, the sense of speech and the sense of hearing are blemished together, as one - and this he was precise about at the end of his words, saying "concerning this it is written, guard your tongue from evil," and so on - for if he speaks evil, that voice enters the ears and shakes the whole body and decrees decrees, and so on - and this is "and the LORD heard, and His anger was kindled."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:10: From here a person shall see how great a blemish reaches one who hears slander and idle words and the other blemishing things with his ears - and to this it says (Ketubot 5b) that he should fold the lobe into it, so that the other senses not suffer harm, especially in light of what is explained there in the Idra, that Chokhmah, Binah, and Da'at are comprised in hearing. And if one speaks slander to his fellow and the like, besides the blemish of speech, he causes his fellow to sin through the blemish of hearing, and also "the LORD hears, and His anger is kindled."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:11: And in the Tikkunim (page 122a) it says that the essence of hearing is on the left, and therefore, if one hears his voice, it should be with fear - in these words: hearing is [for] those who fear God, and concerning it is said (2 Kings 19:16), "incline Your ear, O LORD, and hear," and there is the fear and dread of Isaac, this is what is written (Habakkuk 3:2), "O LORD, I have heard Your report, and I was afraid" - and whoever's voice is heard, whether in Torah, in prayer, or in outcry, without fear, immediately (Numbers 11:1), "and the LORD heard, and His anger was kindled, and the fire of the LORD burned among them" - and how many gatekeepers are there, called the ears of the LORD - to this point. Behold, all the negative aspects that depend on hearing.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:12: And there are also positive aspects, explained in the Tikkunim (page 131b): they said, of blessed memory, and there are precepts that depend on hearing, such as the recitation of the Shema, or other precepts of which it is said (Berachot 15a), "if he made it audible to his own ear, he has fulfilled his obligation" - and this is the blowing of the shofar - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:13: And in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Pinchas, pages 228-229) he says that the repair of hearing is in three aspects: hearing the eighteen blessings from the mouth of the prayer leader and answering "amen" to each and every blessing; hearing the reading of the Torah scroll from the mouth of the reader; hearing his fellow's reasoning in halachah. In these words: the third repair, and those who listen to the Torah scroll at the time speech emerges from the mouth of the reader - it is accounted to them as though they receive the Torah at Mount Sinai, and at the time he says "I am [the LORD your God]," no other voice or speech of any living creature is heard but His - in this manner, when speech emerges from the mouth of the Holy One, blessed be He, the fiery living creatures are silent, and when the fiery speaking living creatures are silent, this is what is written (Exodus 20:15 - actually 20:18), "and all the people saw the voices" - the voices of the living creatures that were roaring - "and the torches" - that would go out in speech through the living creatures in several kinds of melody before the King - and these who listen to the Torah scroll are the images of the living creatures, and the Holy One, blessed be He, appoints them to enter the chamber of the vision of the fire, the house of the LORD. And further, those who listen to the prayer in the eighteen blessings shall enter the chamber of this vision. And further, those who listen to a halachic discussion, of whom it is said, "the reward of hearing a teaching is [good] reasoning," shall enter the chamber that is the palace of this vision - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:14: Further, in the Tikkunim (page 63a), in these words: the fourth offering, this is what receives the offering, corresponding to Adam, which is the thought that offers and unifies everything, and of it is said (Leviticus 1:2), "Adam [man], if he brings an offering of you" - this is what brings an offering to the LORD, and this is Torah - and therefore they established, in prayer, to hear the Torah scroll, so that there be, in it, a complete offering in Adam [man], of which it is said (Numbers 19:14), "this is the Torah, Adam [when a man dies in a tent]" - and therefore, "he who turns away his ear from hearing the Torah, even his prayer is an abomination" - to this point, their wording.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:15: And included in this repair is that sometimes it happens that during the reading of the Torah or prayer, a person speaks with his fellow about worldly matters, and stops listening to the Torah or prayer in order to hear that matter - for he must not incline his ear to hear anything but that very thing to which he first turned his attention to hear, and even if they speak words of Torah, he should not incline his ear, for hearing is like answering - and during the reading of the Torah or during the prayer leader's repetition of the Amidah, it is forbidden for him to occupy himself with Torah, as explained in the teaching. And the general rule is that one should not mix one repair with another, for each has its own time - all the more so if he mixes the profane with the holy, for then the blemish is great.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:16: Further, concerning the repair of hearing, they explained in the Tikkunim (page 122a), in these words: and therefore one must remove hair from over the ears, so that the gates of hearing not be blocked for prayer, for through them He hears prayers, of whom it is said (Psalms 65:3), "O You who hears prayer, to You all flesh shall come" - to this point, their wording.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:17: And the blemish that blemishes smell, which is the nose - without doubt anger and wrath are what blemish it, as they said in the Zohar (Parashat Tetzaveh, page 182a), "cease from man, whose breath is in his nostrils" (Isaiah 2:22). And likewise one should not derive benefit from the smell of idolatry and forbidden foods. And likewise he should distance himself from the smell of a married woman's garments, because it would arouse an evil desire in him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:18: And the repair of smell, he says there in the Tikkunim (page 131b), in these words: and all offerings that are a pleasing aroma to the LORD depend on the nose, and the spice-woods of Havdalah - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:19: And it appears to me that now, because of our sins, since we have no offering, the meditation of our lips shall ascend in place of the aroma, as is known, that they explained, of blessed memory (cf. Menachot 110a), "this is the Torah of the burnt offering, of the meal offering, of the sin offering," and so on (Leviticus 7:37) - one occupied with the Torah of the burnt offering is as though he offered a burnt offering, and so on. And just as through the aroma of the offering satisfaction was given above, as explained in the Idra (Parashat Ha'azinu, page 294a), in the nose of Ze'ir [Anpin] - "and the LORD smelled the pleasing aroma" (Genesis 8:21) - it is not written "the aroma of the offering," but "the pleasing aroma," for all the powers of Gevurah are held in the nose, and all that are joined with them are all sweetened. And he says further there, that upon the altar the fire and the smoke going out from the two nostrils would be sweetened, and the nose of Arich would be revealed, of which it is said (Isaiah 48:9), "I will restrain My anger [lit. hold My nose] for you, for My praise" - and so it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Noach, page 70a) - see there. And if a person sinned through anger and wrath, giving room for the powers of Gevurah to spread, through his occupation with Torah they shall be sweetened and included in their source, and the supernal mercies shall be revealed to sweeten everything - and how good it is if he is fasting, so that the aroma rising from his mouth is in place of an offering, and through the breath of Torah the aroma of his mouth shall ascend above, to unify and sweeten the judgments - for the breath of Torah is a ladder for the ascent of prayer and for the ascent of the soul, as shall be explained in the Gate of Torah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:20: And if he directs his intent in his reading to the act of the offering, that it ascend before the supernal Adam, which is the secret of thought, Yud-Kaf-Yud Vav-Kaf-Yud, that offers everything, as explained above, it is possible that this will also help to repair his thoughts.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:21: And further, concerning the repair of smell, they said in the Tikkunim (page 122a), in these words: smell there is [for] men of truth, and there ascend all aromas, incenses, and smoke of offerings, and prayers accounted as offerings - and if a person does not raise them in love and fear, what is written of him? (Deuteronomy 29:19), "then the anger of the LORD and His jealousy shall smoke against that man" - to this point. Now, from this teaching there is proof for our intent - for it says that prayer, which is in place of an offering, ascends to the nose of Ze'ir to make a pleasing aroma when a person occupies himself with that prayer in fear and love, and if not, Heaven forfend, because of the side of judgment it arouses, "then the anger of the LORD shall smoke," and so on - all the more so one occupied with the Torah of the offering, that it ascend as a pleasing aroma to repair the judgments.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:22: And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, was further precise in his wording, saying, "and there ascend all aromas and incenses," and so on - the intent being that the incense too would ascend to this place to sweeten judgment, and also, if a person reads about the incense with intent, it shall ascend to this place to repair and sweeten the judgments - and at the end of Parashat Vayakhel (page 218b) they elaborated on the virtue of the incense, and we shall copy its wording concerning the matter of prayer, and from there is also proof for our intent.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:23: And what it says, "and if not, they ascend," in love and fear - while above, concerning hearing, it mentioned only fear alone - the reason is that smell is on the central line, as it says, "smell there is [for] men of truth," and the attribute of truth unifies the left and the right, which are fear and love, and therefore the repair of the aroma of prayer, and everything that ascends to the nose, is through fear and love.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:24: And with this the chapter is concluded:
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:1: After we have explained, in the previous chapters, sight, hearing, and smell, which correspond to Yud-Heh-Vav, lion, ox, eagle, as we copied the wording of Rashbi at the beginning of chapter 8, let us now explain speech, which corresponds to the final Heh, and is the face of man.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:2: And the wording of Rashbi there (Ra'aya Meheimna, Parashat Pinchas, page 234a): "speech - man, who holds above and below." And the explanation of these words is explained in what is explained in the Tikkunim (page 122a) concerning the four repairs, which are sight, hearing, smell, speech - it explains there that sight is to the right, lion; hearing to the left, ox; smell in the middle, eagle - and he says afterward, in these words: the mouth, this is man, comprising four letters and comprising ten letters, and this is the Shechinah - to this point. And "comprising four letters," and so on, is the Name YHVH and Yud-Kaf-Yud Vav-Kaf-Yud, and so he explained (page 129a).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:3: And the matter shall be better understood from what he says in the Tikkunim (ibid., page 63a), that lion, ox, eagle are sight, hearing, smell, and upon them rests the supernal face of man, which is the secret of thought - and afterward he says, at the end of his words, "speech, this is man, who comprises them all - who brings it forth? Thought" - to this point. And through this teaching the two previous teachings shall be understood: what it says on page 121, that speech is the Shechinah, and it is in the secret of the simple and full Name spelled with ten [letters] - so it is true, that in it the Name is simple, from the side that it includes the three faces, which are lion, ox, eagle, Yud-Heh-Vav, within it, being the final Heh; and the Name is full with ten, from the secret of the supernal thought, as I elaborated above in chapter 6. And so speech too is found holding above and below - above, in the secret of thought, and below, in the Shechinah - this is the general understanding of the matter.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:4: And in particular, a person does not speak except that he first thinks what he shall speak - rather, it is necessary that that speech be imprinted in thought first, and when he speaks, the power of thought goes out together with that speech - and therefore speech necessarily contains the two Names mentioned together, and this is the secret of (Proverbs 3:19), "the LORD founded the earth with wisdom" - and therefore it is explained in the Tikkunim (page 83a), in these words: Yud is speech, utterance, and reading.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:5: However, it is difficult for me what is said in the Tikkunim, page 3a, that speech is the Name Adonai - and it is possible to say that what is said in the teaching before us, concerning the matter of YHVH simple and full, is entirely the aspect of voice [kol] - and this requires study.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:6: And to understand the matter in its proper composition, it shall be explained by what Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar, Parashat Noach, page 74a), on the verse (1 Kings 6:7), "and the house, when it was built, was built of stone made ready before it was brought there" - he explained this verse concerning the matter of speech, from where its root is, and explained that its root is from the secret of thought, and says: when the desire arises before the Holy One, blessed be He, to make honor for His own honor, will arises from within thought to spread, and so on. And he says [describes] the reality of the spreading of Atzilut until it becomes voice, and says, from where thought, which was sealed in silence, becomes audible so as to be revealed. Further, this thought spreads to become revealed, and this voice strikes and knocks upon the lips, and then speech emerges and completes everything and reveals everything - it is understood that everything is that sealed thought that was within, and everything is one; once this spreading arrives and speech is made with the strength of that voice, then "and the house, when it was built" - "when it was built" is not written, and so on - to this point, relevant here. And whoever wishes to delve into the secret of the matter should examine the teaching in its place there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:7: And similar to this he says in the Zohar (Parashat Vayechi, page 246b), concerning (Genesis 49:21), "Naphtali is a hind let loose, who gives [feminine form] beautiful words" - he explained this verse in the secret of speech, and raised a difficulty that it should have said "hanoten" [masculine "gives"], and answered: come and see, thought is the beginning of everything, and so on - and at the end of his words he says, and when you examine the levels, it is thought, it is Binah, it is voice, it is speech, and all is one, and it is the very thought that is the beginning of everything, and there is no separation, but all is one, and one binding, which is literally thought, bound in Ein [nothing/Ein Sof] and never separated - and this is "the LORD is one and His Name is one" (Zechariah 14:9) - and therefore it is written "hanotenet" [feminine "gives"] - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:8: And through the reason for the secret alluded to, we shall understand what is said in the Zohar (Parashat Chukat, page 183b), that one who guards his mouth and tongue merits to be clothed in the holy spirit, in these words: "and Esther put on royalty" (Esther 5:1) - that she was clothed in the holy supernal royalty, certainly she was clothed in the holy spirit. Why did she merit this place? Because she guarded her mouth not to reveal anything - this is what is written (ibid. 2:20), "Esther did not reveal her kindred" - and we learn that whoever guards his mouth and tongue merits to be clothed in the holy spirit - to this point. And in the Zohar (Parashat Acharei Mot, beginning of page 61), it explains that when it [the Shechinah, "zot"] is called the holy spirit, it is when she nurses from the secret of Chokhmah, in these words, in brief: and this "zot," when she is blessed, is called "kodesh" [holy] and called "Chokhmah," and they called her "the holy spirit" [ru'ach ha-kodesh], meaning a spirit [ru'ach] from that supernal holiness [kodesh] - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:9: And the reason for the word "clothing" [hitlabshut], why one merits the holy spirit through guarding the tongue, shall be explained by what is explained in the Idra (Parashat Naso, page 134a), in the arrangements of the supernal beard, arrangement twelve, where it says that the holy spirit that emerges from the supernal mouth clothes Ze'ir Anpin, and from this spirit all those below are clothed, and so on. And he says afterward: and therefore the spirit that goes out and is clothed by the faithful prophets is called "the fruit of the LORD" - but in this Atika of Atikin [Ancient of Ancients] it is not separated, and none knows His spirit but Him - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:10: And from here you shall know how great is the virtue of one who guards the spirit of breath emerging from his mouth, for it alludes to a supernal place, and therefore he merits to be clothed in the holy spirit. And concerning one who guards his spirit it is said (Proverbs 11:13), "but he who is faithful [ne'eman] in spirit conceals a matter" - and "ne'eman" is explained as being strong in his spirit, not to release it to an unfitting place, and the word "ne'eman" is explained as in (Isaiah 22:23), "and I will fasten him as a peg in a sure [ne'eman] place" - explained as strong, without wavering. And the opposite of this (Proverbs 29:11), "a fool releases all his spirit."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:11: And concerning the punishment of one who blemishes the breath emerging from his mouth, it shall be explained to you by what is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Beshalach, page 59a), concerning (Ecclesiastes 1:14), "all is vanity [hevel] and vexation of spirit" - it says there that it cannot be said that this "hevel" mentioned in the verse refers to something in Atzilut, in the secret of the seven "hevels" [breaths] above in Atzilut, called "the utterance of the mouth of the LORD," as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Tazria, page 47b) - for if it were there, it would not be "vexation of spirit," but rather it is explained to be in the external forces - and he says, in these words: come and see, at the time deeds are made fit below, and a person considers the service of the holy King, that matter he does becomes a "hevel" [breath] from it above, and there is no "hevel" that does not have a voice that ascends and is crowned above and becomes an advocate before the Holy One, blessed be He. But all those deeds a person engages in that are not the service of the Holy One, blessed be He, that matter he does becomes a "hevel" that goes and roams the world, and when a person's soul departs, that "hevel" rolls him about in the world like a stone in a sling, as it is written (1 Samuel 25:29), "and the soul of your enemies He shall sling out from the hollow of the sling" - who slings it out? That "hevel" that leads him about the world. Then all matters done, which are under the sun, that are not the service of the Holy One, blessed be He, a "hevel" is made from them - "hevel" is the breaking of spirit that breaks the spirit and ascends and descends in the world - this is what is written (Ecclesiastes 1:14), "vanity and vexation of spirit." But that matter which is the service of his Master, this is called "above the sun," and a holy "hevel" is made from it, and this is the seed a person sows in that world, and its name is charity, as it is written (Hosea 10:12), "sow for yourselves according to charity" - this leads the person, when his soul departs from him, and raises it up, to be found in the place of glory above, to be bound in the bundle of life - this is what is written (Isaiah 58:8), "and your charity shall go before you" - to lead you, to raise you from place to place, as it is written, "the glory of the LORD shall gather you" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:12: Behold, it is explained in this teaching that every unfitting deed becomes a "hevel" [breath] that clothes the soul and slings it in the hollow of the sling, and it is "vexation of spirit" - and this is what he was precise about in saying, "who slings it, that 'hevel' that leads him about the world" - and in saying "about the world," he alludes to the secret of this matter alluded to. And all the more so when the breath emerging from his mouth is in vain, in falsehood, and the like, going to the place of this evil "hevel," which is "vexation of spirit," and a garment is made from it to clothe his spirit, to sling it within the hollow of the sling.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:13: And in the Tikkunim (page 117b) Rashbi explained the secret of the "hevels" [breaths] on the side of holiness and the "hevels" on the side of the husk - he says there that there is a good "hevel" and an evil "hevel." The "hevel" of Torah is a flame [lahav], of which it is said (Psalms 29:7), "the voice of the LORD hews flames of fire," and this "hevel" is on the right side, comprising seven "hevels" corresponding to the seven names in the Name of forty-two, Alef-Bet-Gimel Yud-Tav-Tzadi, and so on - and he says, six ascend, which are flames, in the six rings of the windpipe, and the seventh "hevel" is of the mouth - and corresponding to them David said, seven voices, "give to the LORD, O sons of the mighty" (Psalms 29:1) - and concerning these seven it is said (Deuteronomy 8:3), "for man does not live by bread alone, but by every utterance of the mouth of the LORD does man live" - and these seven voices ascend in seven firmaments. And there are seven on the left that descend into seven lands, and of them Kohelet says (Ecclesiastes 3:21), "for who knows the spirit of the sons of man, whether it goes upward," and so on (the explanation refers to the end of the verse, "and the spirit of the beast, whether it goes downward to the earth"). Seven good "hevels," these are the seven days of the week corresponding to them, and others correspond to the seven years of famine - these are the "hevels" of life and these are the "hevels" of death, and therefore there is "hevel" [singular] and there are "hevels" [plural] - to this point.
